from.place: Paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation, and the following naturality and triangle-identity sentences; foundational enhancement of finite coefficient adjunction diagrams. Technical input: Pinched simplices give a weakly equivalent mapping resolution. Smaller input: Cone straightening sends right anodyne maps to equivalences and recovers fibers. Item proof: general simplicial-correspondence adjunction used in Steps 1, 2 and 6.

title: Unmarked straightening as a Quillen equivalence for simplicial correspondences
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and the cosimplicial simplicial sets $Q^n=\mathfrak C[(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}](x,y)$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], the Kan model structure (including Kan fibrations) of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the contravariant model structure and model-generation conventions of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$, a small simplicial category $D$, and a simplicial functor $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $a:X\to S$ let $v$ be a new vertex and put $M_{a,\phi}=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}D^{\mathrm{op}}$, using $\phi\mathfrak C[a]$ as the second attaching map; the join is the ordered cone with its last vertex $v$. Define $L_\phi(X)(d)=M_{a,\phi}(d,v)$, with the $D$-action given by precomposition. Define the simplicial set $U_\phi(F)$ over $S$ by declaring that its $n$-simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are enriched natural transformations $L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to F$. Operators are restriction along simplex operators. Here an enriched natural transformation has simplicial maps at objects satisfying the action-square equality.

The category of simplicial functors $D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and enriched natural transformations has a cofibrantly generated projective model structure with functorial factorizations: weak equivalences and fibrations are respectively objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations, and cofibrations are maps with the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations. The displayed constructions are an adjunction $L_\phi\dashv U_\phi$; $L_\phi$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. If $\phi$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set and an equivalence on the categories obtained by taking components of mapping simplicial sets, this adjunction is a Quillen equivalence: for every $X\to S$ and every projectively fibrant $F$, a map $L_\phi X\to F$ is a projective weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to U_\phi F$ is a contravariant weak equivalence. Moreover $U_\phi F\to S$ is a right fibration whenever $F$ is projectively fibrant.

For every $F$ and $s\in S_0$ there is a natural simplicial isomorphism $(U_\phi F)_s\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q(F(\phi(s)))$, where $\operatorname{Sing}_Q(T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,T)$. Under this isomorphism the restriction to a fiber of an adjoint map $X\to U_\phi F$ is adjoint to the composite $|X_s|_Q\to(L_\phi X)(\phi(s))\to F(\phi(s))$; for every simplicial set $K$, define $|K|_Q=\int^{[n]}K_n\times Q^n$ as the quotient of $\coprod_nK_n\times Q^n$ by $(K(\alpha)(z),q)\sim(z,Q(\alpha)(q))$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $z\in K_n$ and $q\in Q^m$. The first arrow of that composite is induced by the fiber inclusion into the ordered cone. Here trivial means also a weak equivalence, and projectively fibrant means that every value is a Kan complex. No quasicategory assumption on $S$ or local Kan assumption on $D$ is made.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and Theorem 2.2.1.2, proved via Proposition 2.2.3.11; Remark 2.2.2.11 for the strict fiber identification; Section A.3.3 for the projective model structure. No Stacks tag states unmarked straightening.

proof.text: The first assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] says that the Kan model category is combinatorial and simplicial. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] with this model category and the small simplicial category $D$. This gives the enriched projective model structure with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations; it is combinatorial, so its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems are generated by small sets $I_D$ and $J_D$. Thus the trivial fibrations are exactly the $I_D$-injective maps and the fibrations exactly the $J_D$-injective maps. For the cellular functorial factorizations required by the generation convention, run the small object argument: by [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] each domain of a map in $I_D\cup J_D$ has an infinite regular presentability rank; these domains form a small family, so [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] gives an infinite regular $\lambda$ exceeding all these ranks. A continuous chain indexed by the initial ordinal of $\lambda$ is $\lambda$-filtered, hence filtered for every smaller rank, so the Hom functor of every domain preserves it. Hence [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] applies to $I_D$ and to $J_D$ and gives functorial factorizations as an $I_D$-cell (resp. $J_D$-cell) map followed by an $I_D$-injective (resp. $J_D$-injective) map. In particular its cofibrations are exactly the maps lifting against objectwise trivial fibrations. The same construction applies to $A=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Neither application requires local Kan mapping objects.

Put $A=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\psi=\phi^{\mathrm{op}}:A\to D$. The identity-base cone functor $T_S$ and its ordinary right adjoint $U_S$ are specified by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. For an $A$-diagram $G$, construct $\psi_!G$ at $d$ as the enriched coend $\int^{a\in A}D(\psi a,d)\times G(a)$, the quotient by the two action maps. Maps from this coend to $F(d)$, natural in $d$, correspond to enriched natural maps $G\to\psi^*F$: evaluation at $1_{\psi a}$ and application of the $D$-action are mutually inverse, by the unit and associativity equations. Thus $\psi_!\dashv\psi^*$. No nonidentity arrow leaves the new cone vertex. Paths from an old object to it in the pushout consist of an old arrow followed by a cone arrow, with precisely the coend action relations; hence $L_\phi=\psi_!T_S$. Composing adjunction bijections gives $L_\phi\dashv U_S\psi^*$. Evaluation on each simplex over $S$ identifies this right adjoint with the displayed $U_\phi$, compatibly with simplex operators.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and Proposition 2.2.1.1(2); coend universal property expanded explicitly.

proof.text: Two contravariant model structures on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ are stated in the DAG: the one of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], with weak equivalences defined by mapping complexes into right fibrations, and the one of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model], with weak equivalences defined by cone categorical equivalences, which is the one named in the statement. Both have the monomorphisms (degreewise injections) as cofibrations, and in both the fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations over $S$. By [lem-coef-model-structure-determined-by-fibrant-objects] they have the same weak equivalences and fibrations, hence the same trivial cofibrations; below, contravariant weak equivalences, trivial cofibrations and Quillen statements from either node are used interchangeably. By [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], $T_S$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations in the contravariant model. Restriction $\psi^*$ preserves objectwise fibrations and trivial fibrations. Its adjunction therefore implies that $\psi_!$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations: a lifting square against a trivial fibration, respectively fibration, becomes a lifting square against its restriction. Hence the composite $L_\phi=\psi_!T_S$ has both preservation properties. A right Quillen functor preserves fibrant objects, since it preserves the terminal object and fibrations to it. Thus $U_\phi F\to S$ is fibrant, and [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] identifies it as a right fibration.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, Quillen-adjunction part, and Proposition A.3.3.7(1).

proof.text: Suppose that $\phi$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Reversal of the mapping objects and composition makes $\psi$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence as well. Apply the change-of-indexing criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] to obtain the Quillen equivalence $\psi_!\dashv\psi^*$. Every $X\to S$ is cofibrant, since the initial map is degreewise injective and [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] identifies these maps as cofibrations. Consequently $T_SX$ is projectively cofibrant by Step 3. If $F$ is projectively fibrant, so is $\psi^*F$. For an actual map $f:\psi_!T_SX\to F$, the change-of-indexing criterion says that $f$ is a weak equivalence precisely when its adjoint $g:T_SX\to\psi^*F$ is one. The identity-base Quillen equivalence in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] says that $g$ is a weak equivalence precisely when its adjoint $h:X\to U_S\psi^*F$ is one. Step 2 identifies $h$ with the stated adjoint under $L_\phi\dashv U_\phi$. By the comparison of the two contravariant model structures in Step 3, via [lem-coef-model-structure-determined-by-fibrant-objects], $h$ is a weak equivalence of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] exactly when it is a contravariant weak equivalence of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. This proves the required criterion without replacing the actual map by a different one.

source.place: Completion of Theorem 2.2.1.2 after Proposition 2.2.3.11, using Proposition A.3.3.8.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $s$ and use the constant simplex $\Delta^n\to\{s\}\to S$. In its cone pushout the whole initial face maps constantly to $\phi(s)$, including all its mapping simplices. Collapsing that face first gives the pinched simplex $J^n$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], whose sole new mapping set is $Q^n$. Attaching its object $x$ to $\phi(s)$ then gives $L_\phi(\Delta^n\to s)(d)=D(\phi(s),d)\times Q^n$: each new arrow is uniquely an old arrow followed, in the opposite category, by an element of $Q^n$. An enriched natural map from this diagram to $F$ is uniquely determined by a simplicial map $q:Q^n\to F(\phi(s))$; at $d$ its value is $(g,z)\mapsto F(g)(q(z))$, and its inverse evaluates at $g=1_{\phi(s)}$. These mutually inverse descriptions commute with simplex operators because the pinched construction does. Applying the simplex definition of $U_\phi$ gives the required natural strict fiber isomorphism for every $F$, without a fibrancy condition.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.11, using the construction of Q in Section 2.2.2; enriched representable calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: Let $f:L_\phi X\to F$ and let $h:X\to U_\phi F$ be its adjoint. For $z\in (X_s)_n$, the simplex $h(z)$ is the enriched natural map obtained by composing $L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{z}X)\to L_\phi X$ with $f$. By Step 5 its fiber value is the map $Q^n\to F(\phi(s))$ obtained by evaluating on the identity arrow. The adjoint on the coend $|X_s|_Q$ therefore sends the generator $(z,q)$ to this value at $q$. This is exactly the composite induced by the fiber inclusion into the cone followed by $f(\phi(s))$. Write $e_z:Q^n\to F(\phi(s))$ for this evaluation map. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, restriction in the definition of $U_\phi$ gives $e_{X_s(\alpha)(z)}=e_z\circ Q(\alpha)$. Therefore the two representatives $(X_s(\alpha)(z),q)$ and $(z,Q(\alpha)(q))$ have the same image, namely $e_z(Q(\alpha)(q))$. The two maps consequently descend to the same simplicial map from the stated quotient. For a map $b:X\to X^\prime$ over $S$, precomposition replaces $e_z$ by $e_{b(z)}$; for an enriched natural map $c:F\to F^\prime$, postcomposition replaces it by $c_{\phi(s)}e_z$. These formulas prove naturality in both arguments.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.11 and the defining adjunction; equality on the generators of the coend quotient.

lean.statement: theorem unmarked_straightening_quillen (S : SSet.{u}) (D : SCat.{u}) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D) : HasProjectiveModel D ∧ ∃ (L : Over S ⥤ Diagram D) (U : Diagram D ⥤ Over S) (hL : IsStraightening D φ L) (description : SimplexDescription D L U) (adj : L ⊣ U), IsConeAdjunction description adj ∧ (∀ (X Y : Over S) (f : X ⟶ Y), Mono f.left → projectiveCof D (L.map f)) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Over S) (f : X ⟶ Y), Mono f.left → contravariantWeak S f → projectiveWeak D (L.map f)) ∧ (Bergner.dwyerKanEquivalences φ → ∀ (X : Over S) (F : Diagram D), ProjectivelyFibrant F → ∀ f : L.obj X ⟶ F, projectiveWeak D f ↔ contravariantWeak S ((adj.homEquiv X F) f)) ∧ (∀ F : Diagram D, ProjectivelyFibrant F → Enhanced.rightFibration (U.obj F).hom) ∧ ∃ (g : PinchedGenerators D φ) (fiberIso : ∀ (F : Diagram D) (s : S _⦋0⦌), Enhanced.fiber (U.obj F).hom s ≅ singQ (F.functor.obj (coefficientVertex D φ s))) (comparison : ∀ (X : Over S) (s : S _⦋0⦌), qRealization (Enhanced.fiber X.hom s) ⟶ value D φ X (coefficientVertex D φ s)), (∀ (F G : Diagram D) (f : F ⟶ G) (s : S _⦋0⦌), Enhanced.fiberMap (U.map f) s ≫ (fiberIso G s).hom = (fiberIso F s).hom ≫ singQMap (f.app (coefficientVertex D φ s))) ∧ (∀ (X : Over S) (s : S _⦋0⦌) (n : SimplexCategory) (z : (Enhanced.fiber X.hom s).obj (op n)), qGenerator n z ≫ comparison X s = pinchedValueMap g n.len s ≫ valueMap D φ (fiberSimplexArrow X s n z) (coefficientVertex D φ s)) ∧ ∀ (X : Over S) (F : Diagram D) (f : L.obj X ⟶ F) (s : S _⦋0⦌), Enhanced.fiberMap ((adj.homEquiv X F) f) s ≫ (fiberIso F s).hom = qAdjunct (comparison X s ≫ eqToHom (hL.obj_eq X (coefficientVertex D φ s)).symm ≫ f.app (coefficientVertex D φ s))
lean.note: The canonical functors and adjunction are existential witnesses fully specified on objects, full simplicial actions, arrows, simplices, simplex operators and the simplexwise adjunction formula. No functor or other data are selected from this theorem. Strict enriched transformations wrap the existing Mathlib GradedNatTrans at the tensor unit; their simplicial components are obtained by uncurrying. Named proof-only helpers translate its full enriched square to the component action square and back and give component extensionality. Mathlib EnrichedNatTrans only stores ordinary naturality and is not the arrow type. Q-realization is a degreewise quotient by all coend relations. PinchedGenerators normalizes the auxiliary maps on the uncollapsed simplex and the surjective Q quotient; comparison is normalized on every quotient summand induced by the strict fiber inclusion. The fiber-adjunction identity is an equality of simplicial maps, for every F without fibrancy. No dependency records or stage-1 proof fields change.
